defect: Skipping the leading text of the first identifier when the expression's AST node is a TypeScript node drops characters that are not part of a type assertion. The non-null assertion operator `!` is one: templates using it stopped compiling, and projects failed their build. vuejs/core reverted this in #14062, closing issue #14060 ("Regression in 3.5.23: fails to parse ! in typescript"). The revert is the ground truth; nothing about the defect was written here.
why_it_is_hard: `TS_NODE_TYPES` is an existing exported constant and the guard reads as reusing the codebase's own notion of a TypeScript node. The bug is that the set is broader than the case being fixed, and the consequence — a whole operator ceasing to compile — is invisible from a diff that adds a conditional and a passing test.

pinned_repository.subject: fix(compiler-core): correctly handle ts type assertions in expressions (#13397)

notes: Shipped in a release and found by users building real projects. The repository's own suite passes.
